title: ChipAgent The Full Stack: Past the Demo
gist: A short SemiWiki forum promotion for a ChipAgents video interview, 'The Full Stack: Past the Demo,' framing the gap between impressive AI demos and production deployment in chip design and verification. The listed talking points — benchmark inadequacy for long-horizon tasks, coverage closure, formal verification, legacy codebase comprehension, secure deployment and month-to-days workflow compression — map the actual objections agentic EDA vendors must answer.

insights.claim: AI for semiconductor design can look impressive in a demo, but making agentic AI work in real-world chip design and verification workflows is a separate and harder problem.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: The vendor-side framing concedes that demos are not evidence — use production deployment references, not demos, when underwriting agentic EDA claims.
insights.quote: AI for semiconductor design can look impressive in a demo, but what does it take to make agentic AI work in real-world chip design and verification workflows?
insights.locator: AI for semiconductor design can look impressive

insights.claim: Traditional AI benchmarks fall short for complex, long-horizon engineering tasks, which is the first issue ChipAgents raises about deploying AI in semiconductor engineering.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Published model benchmark scores are a poor proxy for value in EDA workloads; look for task-completion metrics on real design flows instead.
insights.quote: Why traditional AI benchmarks fall short for complex, long-horizon engineering tasks
insights.locator: In The Full Stack: Past the Demo

insights.claim: Secure, reliable deployment across production engineering teams is called out as a distinct requirement separate from raw AI capability in semiconductor workflows.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Security and IP-containment terms are a gating factor for enterprise adoption of AI in chip design — a common reason pilots stall before scaling.
insights.locator: What it takes to deploy AI securely and reliably

insights.claim: ChipAgents positions agentic AI against specific verification workloads — coverage closure, formal verification, debugging and root cause analysis — rather than generic design assistance.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Verification is the largest and most labor-intensive slice of design cost, so these are the workloads where measurable ROI — and incumbent displacement — would first show up.
insights.locator: How agentic AI approaches coverage closure

insights.claim: A distinct claimed capability is capturing institutional knowledge and understanding legacy semiconductor codebases, positioning AI as a remedy for undocumented, aging design IP.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Legacy-IP comprehension is a switching-cost-creating feature: once agents encode a firm's design history, the tooling becomes hard to displace.
insights.quote: How AI can capture institutional knowledge and understand legacy semiconductor codebases
insights.locator: How AI can capture institutional knowledge

insights.claim: The productivity claim on offer is that close collaboration between engineers and AI can compress month-long workflows into days, with the endpoint framed as an AI-native EDA workflow running from intent to tape-out.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A month-to-days compression claim is the number to test against customer references; if real at scale it reprices design-services labor and shortens product cycles.
insights.quote: How close collaboration between engineers and AI can compress month-long workflows into days
insights.locator: How close collaboration between engineers and AI
